subject: Marketplace reseller addendum — signer path, liability carveouts, and redline tracker
messages:
From: Aaron Lim <aaron.lim@helixcloud.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helix Cloud Contracts <contracts@helixcloud.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Marketplace reseller addendum - pass-through liability and signer path

Hi Vivek / Laura —

Thanks for the earlier sync. Attached is the initial addendum (Helix-Redwood_MSAAmendment_v1.docx) we discussed for listing Redwood on the Helix Marketplace. Two quick asks from our side:

1) Pass-through liability: Helix prefers carveouts where marketplace fees are passed through to the reseller rather than Helix taking on primary VAT/VAT-withholding liabilities. Can Redwood confirm if it can accept a pass-through position (seller retains collection responsibility) or if Redwood needs the platform to withhold locally?

2) Signer path: Our procurement team requires the following signer sequence — Helix legal -> Helix VP Sales -> Redwood CEO. If Redwood needs a different ordering, flag now so we can set the DocuSign route.

We want to move quickly (target: complete addendum in 10 business days). Please confirm who on Redwood will be the signing authority and send any redlines back.

Attachments: Helix-Redwood_MSAAmendment_v1.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Aaron Lim
Head of Partnerships, Helix Cloud
aaron.lim@helixcloud.com

--

Subject: Re: Marketplace reseller addendum - pass-through liability and signer path

Aaron —

Appreciate the draft. Quick response from Redwood:

- Signer authority: Redwood recommends countersignature by our Head of Partnerships (Ben Carter) followed by our General Counsel if legal signoff is needed; for deal values under $250k Ben can countersign without CEO signature. If Helix requires CEO countersign, please confirm.
- Pass-through liability: we need our tax team and legal to review the proposed carveouts. In practice we often accept pass-through for transaction fees but have to be careful about indemnity language that could create open-ended liability.

I’m looping in Ben (ops/partnerships) and Laura (sales ops), and we’ll bring legal into the thread (expect an internal redline and commentary later today).

Next steps proposed:
1) Redwood to share an initial redline (high level — commercial and tax flags).
2) Exchange a brief mutual action plan with signer sequence and target dates.
3) If redlines are small, proceed with DocuSign envelope with signer order agreed.

I’ve attached a one-page summary of our commercial flags (redlines_kulkarni_v1.pdf).

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Revenue, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Marketplace reseller addendum - pass-through liability and signer path

Folks —

I reviewed Helix's v1 addendum and put together marked language (redline_markup_kpark.docx). High-level legal positions below (redline highlights in the docx):

1) Liability / Indemnity: We can accept a pass-through approach for marketplace transaction fees (i.e., marketplace collects and remits VAT/sales tax on its own account) only if:
   - Helix expressly limits indemnity to losses caused by Helix's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
   - Any payments the marketplace withholds for tax are shadowed by a requirement to provide tax receipts/withholding certificates to Redwood and our reseller customers within 60 days.

2) Audit window: Helix proposes a 90-day audit window for pass-through chargebacks. Redwood requests a 30-day initial window with a 12-month rolling reconciliation right for systemic issues. Compromise language proposed in redline.

3) Signer path: We are OK with Helix's suggested sequencing as long as the DocuSign envelope supports conditional routing (in case VP Sales isn't available); alternatively, Helix can allow Countersign by Head of Partnerships (Ben) and then GC if thresholds breached.

4) Data residency & logs: Since resale activity can create audit risk, Helix must commit to preserving transactional logs for 18 months and provide access for bona fide audits (redline includes minimal SOC-type references).

Attaching the redline; please confirm whether Helix legal can accept the limited indemnity carve (we cannot agree to open-ended pass-through exposure). Also cc'ing their contracts mailbox to keep procurement in the loop.

Attachments: redline_markup_kpark.docx (docx)

-Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Kimberly / Vivek —

Thanks for the thorough read and the proposed language. Helix is comfortable with the limited indemnity carve you suggested (gross negligence/willful misconduct) and we can provide withholding certificates within 30 days of request — that should be workable.

On the audit window: Helix prefers 60 days for initial chargeback disputes. We can accept Redwood's 12-month reconciliation right for systemic issues as long as we limit ad hoc audits to a quarterly cadence.

Signer path — confirmed: Helix will route internal signers first (Helix legal -> Helix VP Sales) and then send to Redwood for countersign by Ben Carter (Head of Partnerships). If Ben is unavailable, route to Redwood GC (Kimberly Park) as backup.

Please send the DocuSign envelope and a short mutual action plan with target dates. Proposed timeline:
- Final redline exchange: 2 business days
- DocuSign routing & signatures: 3 business days
- Live marketplace listing: +5 business days post-signature

I’ll ask our contracts mailbox to open the DocuSign envelope and share the link here.

Thanks,
Aaron Lim
Head of Partnerships, Helix Cloud
